'''''Astilbe chinensis''''', commonly known as '''false goat's beard''',<ref>{{Cite book|url=http://www.forest.go.kr/kna/special/download/English_Names_for_Korean_Native_Plants.pdf |title=English Names for Korean Native Plants |publisher=[[Korea National Arboretum]] |year=2015 |isbn=978-89-97450-98-5 |location=Pocheon |pages=385 |access-date=25 January 2016 |via=[[Korea Forest Service]] |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170525105020/http://www.forest.go.kr/kna/special/download/English_Names_for_Korean_Native_Plants.pdf |archivedate=25 May 2017 }}</ref> '''tall false-buck's-beard'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=17 October 2014 }}</ref> or '''Chinese astilbe''',<ref name=missouri/> is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the [[saxifrage]] family, [[Saxifragaceae]].<ref name=POWO>{{cite taxon |POWO |id=790271-1 |title=''Astilbe chinensis'' (Maxim.) Franch. & Sav. |access-date=March 16, 2026}}</ref> It is a perennial herb that grows near shaded streams and rivers. It is also commonly grown in [[shade garden]]s.

== Taxonomy ==

The [[binomial name]] of Chinese astilbe is ''Astilbe chinensis''. The [[genus name]], ''Astilbe'', from the Greek words for "without" and "brightness", refers to the dullness of leaves of some species, while the [[specific epithet]] refers to the plant's Chinese origin.<ref name=missouri/>

Chinese astilbe was originally described as ''Hoteia chinensis'' by C. J. Maximowiez in 1859. In 1875, [[Adrien René Franchet]] and [[Ludovic Savatier]] transferred it to the genus ''[[Astilbe]]''.<ref name=Lauener/> Whether ''A. chinensis'' and ''A. rubra'' were distinct species or [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonyms]] was a controversial issue for botanists throughout the 20th century,<ref name=Lauener>{{Cite book|first=L. A.|last=Lauener|publisher=SPB Academic Publications|page=28|year=1996|title=The introduction of Chinese plants into Europe}}</ref> with current consensus favoring the latter interpretation.<ref name=theplantlist>{{Cite web|url=http://www.theplantlist.org/tpl1.1/record/kew-2656798|title=Astilbe rubra Hook.f. & Thomson|publisher=[[The Plant List]]}}</ref> The plant once known as ''Astilbe davidii'' <small>(Franch.)</small> is today regarded as a [[variety (botany)|variety]] of ''A. chinensis''. Other varieties include ''A. chinensis'' var. ''divaricata'' <small>(Nakai)</small> and ''A. chinensis'' var. ''pumila'' <small>(auct.)</small>.<ref name=theplantlist/>

==Description==
''Astilbe chinensis'' is a [[herbaceous]] [[perennial]] growing in clumps.<ref name=missouri/> The species reaches a height of {{convert|45|–|90|cm}}.<ref name=Lauener/> The leaves are predominantly [[basal leaf|basal]] and ternately [[compound leaves|compound]] with sharply-toothed (often biserrated) [[Leaflet (botany)|leaflets]]. Most leaflets are elliptic to oval in shape and hairy. The mounds of leaves resemble [[ferns]]. Flowers are minuscule and form [[panicle]]s on thin, erect or arching stems.<ref name=missouri>{{Cite web|url=http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=h400|publisher=[[Missouri Botanical Garden]]|title=Astilbe chinensis 'Visions'|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130926055942/http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=h400|archivedate=26 September 2013|url-status=live|access-date=12 April 2019}}</ref>

== Distribution and habitat ==

Chinese astilbe was discovered by [[Richard Maack]] on 6 July 1855 in the south of modern-day [[Amur Oblast]] of Russia and the Chinese region [[Heilongjiang]], and by [[Leopold von Schrenck]] the following year.<ref name=Lauener/> The natural range of Chinese astilbe is [[Eastern China]], [[Japanese archipelago]], and [[Korea]], at altitudes between 400 and 3600 meters. It is found along shaded streams and rivers as well as within and along the margins of damp, open [[broadleaf forest]]s.<ref name=pfaf>{{Cite web|url=https://pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Astilbe+chinensis|publisher=[[Plants for a Future]]|title=Astilbe chinensis – (Maxim.)Franch.&Sav. }}</ref>

== Cultivation ==

Chinese astilbe is prized for its attractive foliage, plume-like inflorescence in the summer, and dried seed heads afterwards.<ref name=missouri/> In 1902, the ''[[Journal of the Royal Horticultural Society]]'' described it as "the most important hardy perennial introduced during the past few years".<ref name=Lauener/> Chinese astilbe is usually planted in [[woodland garden]]s and shaded parts of [[herbaceous border]]s or [[cottage garden]]s as [[groundcover]] or edging plant. The plant requires partial to full shade, and grows best in soil which is well-drained and rich in organic material. While more tolerant of drought and exposure to direct sunlight than its [[congener (biology)|congeners]], the soil must never dry out. Generally resistant to pathogens and herbivores, most problems are caused by high temperatures and drought.<ref name=missouri/>

The following [[cultivar]]s have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]]:
*''A. chinensis'' var. ''pumila'' - mauve<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Astilbe chinensis'' var. ''pumila''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/54603/Astilbe-chinensis-var-pumila/Details | accessdate=15 April 2020}}</ref> 
*''A. chinensis'' var. ''taqueti'' 'Purpurlanze' - red/purple<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/112790/Astilbe-chinensis-var-taquetii-Purpurlanze/Details | title = ''A. chinensis'' var. ''taqueti'' 'Purpulanze' | publisher = RHS | accessdate = 12 April 2020}}</ref> 
*''A. chinensis'' var. ''taqueti'' 'Superba'<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/89593/Astilbe-chinensis-var-taquetii-Superba/Details | title = ''A. chinensis'' var. taqueti 'Superba' | publisher = RHS | accessdate = 12 April 2020}}</ref> - rose/mauve
